337558.title: Divisibility refinement for symmetric groups of prime-power degree
337558.literal_statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $a\in\mathbb{N}$, let $S_{p^a}$ be the symmetric group on $p^a$ elements, and let $P$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $S_{p^a}$. Let $\operatorname{N}_{S_{p^a}}(P)$ be its normalizer, and let $\operatorname{Irr}_{p'}(S_{p^a})$ denote the irreducible characters of $S_{p^a}$ whose degrees are not divisible by $p$. **Prime-power symmetric-group conjecture.** There exists a bijection

$$
f:\operatorname{Irr}_{p'}(S_{p^a})\longrightarrow \operatorname{Irr}_{p'}(\operatorname{N}_{S_{p^a}}(P))
$$

such that

$$
f(\chi)(1)\mid\chi(1)\quad\text{for all }\chi\in\operatorname{Irr}(S_{p^a}).
$$

This generalizes the proposed prime-degree assertion. The source reports bijections for the first few primes and powers, but notes computational limitations and gives no proof or counterexample.

Literal final universal Irr quantifier exceeds displayed domain; do not credit that domain correction. Next: restore source bijection quantifier and hook-degree divisibility mechanism.

337569.title: Migliore–Miro-Roig conjecture on ghost terms in resolutions of generic forms
337569.literal_statement:
Let $S=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, and let $I\subset S$ be generated by $d>n$ generic forms of the same degree. A redundant term in a minimal free resolution means a free summand occurring in two different homological degrees with the same internal shift.

**Migliore–Miro-Roig conjecture.** The minimal free resolution of $S/I$ has no redundant term. Consequently, the minimal free resolution is the minimum one consistent with the Hilbert function.

The conjecture concerns whether generic equal-degree generators can produce ghost terms in their minimal resolutions. The source gives no resolution status.
337569.reason_and_next_lemma: Generic equal-degree minimal resolutions: no finite exact genericity certificate or full syzygy construction identified. Next: source characteristic/genericity assumptions and an explicit universally generic ghost-term mechanism.

337604.title: The even-cycle multigraph host conjecture
337604.literal_statement:
Let $=$ be the family of even cycles, and let $_^*(k)$ denote the maximum number of edges in a host multigraph $G$ with $(G,)<k$.

**Even-cycle multigraph conjecture.** For $k\geq 6$,

$$
_^*(k)=\left\lfloor\frac{k^2}{4}\right\rfloor,
$$

and $K_{\lfloor k/2\rfloor,\lceil k/2\rceil}$ is also the unique extremal graph for $_^*(k)$.
The corresponding assertion for simple host graphs is proved in the paper, whereas the multigraph version is presented as unresolved because the simple-graph argument does not apply to multigraphs.

337625.title: Conjecture on dimension two for open convex codes
337625.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a convex open code, meaning a code realizable by open convex sets. Its **minimal convex embedding dimension** is the smallest dimension in which it is realizable by convex sets, and its **minimal open convex embedding dimension** is the smallest dimension in which it is realizable by open convex sets.

**Dimension-two embedding conjecture.** If $\mathcal{C}$ has minimal open convex embedding dimension $2$, then its minimal convex embedding dimension is $2$.

This is stated as equivalent to the dimension-one conjecture above. It would show that, for open convex codes whose least open realization dimension is two, allowing non-open convex realizations does not reduce the dimension.

337633.title: Last-row Schur module conjecture for the Veronese surface
337633.literal_statement:
For the $d$-uple Veronese embedding of $\mathbb P^2$, let $p:=d\binom{d+1}{2}$ and define

$$
(a,b,c)=\left(\binom{d+2}{3}-1,\frac{1}{6}d(d^2+5),\binom{d+1}{3}-1\right).
$$

**Last-row Schur module conjecture.** The last nonzero syzygy space is

$$
K_{p,p+1}(\mathbb P^2,0;d)\cong \mathbf S_{(a,b,c)}.
$$

This gives a Schur-functor analogue of a corresponding conjecture cited in the source; the specified $p$ is the maximum value for which $K_{p,p+1}(0;d)\ne0$. The paper presents this as a conjecture based on data, with no general proof stated.

337684.title: Authors' classification conjecture for non-bipartite distance-regular graphs
337684.literal_statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a non-bipartite distance-regular graph with valency $k$, diameter $D$, and smallest eigenvalue $\theta_{\min}\leq -k/2$. The graph is assumed to have sufficiently large diameter.

**Authors' classification conjecture.** When $D$ is large enough, $\Gamma$ is one of the following graphs: the odd polygons; folded $(2D+1)$-cubes; the odd graphs $O_k$; the Hamming graphs $H(D,3)$; the dual polar graphs $^2A_{2D-1}(2)$; or the dual polar graphs $B_D(2)$.

This conjecture proposes a classification of non-bipartite distance-regular graphs under a smallest-eigenvalue bound. The source notes that it is correct when both $c_2\geq 3$ and $a_1=1$ hold, while the general large-diameter case remains open.
337684.reason_and_next_lemma: Sufficiently-large-diameter classification, not a single exceptional graph. No arbitrarily-large-diameter nonlisted family or full classification mechanism found.

337690.title: Flag lower-bound conjecture for edges of simplicial spheres
337690.literal_statement: Fix positive integers $n$ and $m$, and consider flag triangulations of the $(n-1)$-dimensional sphere with $m$ vertices. Let the $(n-2)$-fold suspension of the one-dimensional sphere with $m-2n+4$ vertices be the specified comparison complex. **Flag edge lower-bound conjecture.** Among all flag triangulations of the $(n-1)$-dimensional sphere with a given number $m$ of vertices, the $(n-2)$-fold suspension over the one-dimensional sphere with $m-2n+4$ vertices has the smallest possible number of edges. This conjecture is presented as equivalent to the nonnegativity of the second $gamma$-coefficient in Gal's conjecture and concerns a flag analogue of Barnette's Lower Bound Theorem; the source gives no resolution.

337698.title: Non-torsion primitive-point conjecture for large almost simple Galois extensions
337698.literal_statement:
Let $C/K$ be a smooth, projective, hyperelliptic curve of genus $g\geq 1$ with a $K$-rational point $P_0$, and embed $C$ into its Jacobian $J_C$ using $P_0$. Let $L/K$ be a finite Galois extension, write $G=\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$, and let $P\in C(L)$ be **$L$-primitive** if $L$ is the smallest Galois extension of $K$ over which $P$ is defined. Let $m(G)$ denote the quantity used in the source. **The non-torsion primitive-point conjecture.** If $G$ is nonabelian almost simple and $|G|$ is sufficiently large, then $P$ is non-torsion in $J_C(L)$; in particular,

$$
\dim J_C(L)\otimes\mathbb Q\geq m(G).
$$

The conjecture connects large nonabelian Galois groups of fields of definition with Jacobian rank; it is explicitly described as very optimistic and remains open in the source.

337733.title: The characterization conjecture for Krull monoids by systems of sets of lengths
337733.literal_statement:
Let $M$ and $M'$ be Krull monoids with respective finite abelian class groups $G$ and $G'$, and suppose that each class of both groups contains at least one prime divisor. Assume also that $\mathsf{D}(G)\geq 4$.

**Characterization conjecture.** If

$$
\mathcal{L}(M)=\mathcal{L}(M'),
$$

then $M\cong M'$.

This is the Characterization Problem in factorization theory: whether systems of sets of lengths determine Krull monoids under these hypotheses. The source states that the conjecture remains open, although it is known under certain additional conditions.

337776.title: Ax–Schanuel conjecture for variations of mixed integral Hodge structures
337776.literal_statement:
Let $(S,\mathbb{V})$ be a $\mathbb{Z}$VMHS, let $U\subset\widetilde S\times S$ be an algebraic subvariety, and let $W$ be an irreducible component of $U\cap\Delta$, where $\Delta$ is the graph of $\pi:\widetilde S\longrightarrow S$. **Ax–Schanuel for $\mathbb{Z}$VMHS.** Then

$$
\operatorname{cd}_U W\geq \dim \overline{W}^{\mathrm{ws}},
$$

where $\overline{W}^{\mathrm{ws}}$ denotes the smallest weakly special subvariety of $S$ containing $\pi(W)$. This is identified as the main functional-transcendence conjecture for variations of mixed integral Hodge structures; no resolution is given in the source.
337776.reason_and_next_lemma: Mixed-VMHS functional transcendence requires period-map definitions and weakly-special closures. No primary proof-body review or claimed novelty clearance; next compare actual later mixed Ax-Schanuel theorems.

337828.title: Canonical lift volume-minimizing conjecture for filling closed geodesics
337828.literal_statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a hyperbolic surface, let $\gamma$ be a filling closed geodesic on $\Sigma$, let $\hat{\gamma}$ denote its canonical lift, and let $M_{\tilde{\gamma}}$ be the complement associated with a lift $\tilde{\gamma}\to\gamma$. **Canonical lift volume-minimizing conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{Vol}(M_{\hat{\gamma}})=\min_{\tilde{\gamma}\to\gamma}\{\operatorname{Vol}(M_{\tilde{\gamma}})\}.
$$

The conjecture asks whether the canonical lift complement has the smallest volume among all lift complements of a fixed filling closed geodesic. Continuous lift complements are hyperbolic $3$-manifolds of finite volume, but the minimization assertion is left as a question.
337828.reason_and_next_lemma: Volume infimum over lift complements requires hyperbolic lift class and volume comparison. No certified full-scope topological construction.

337846.title: Global isoperimetric conjecture for centered circles in the Holmes–Thompson plane
337846.literal_statement:
Let $(F_B,B^2(1))$ be the two-dimensional Finsler space form under consideration, and let $c_0$ be the circle centered at the origin. Consider simple closed curves that are smooth and have a fixed length.

**Global Holmes–Thompson isoperimetric conjecture.** The circle $c_0$ encloses the maximal Holmes–Thompson area among all such curves.

The preceding result establishes that $c_0$ is a proper strong maximum of the isoperimetric problem and that there are no conjugate points along the isoperimetric extremal circles. The conjecture asserts that this local maximality extends to a global maximum.

337879.title: The vertex-maximum-clique criterion for weakly perfect graphs
337879.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a **weakly perfect graph**, meaning that its clique number and chromatic number agree, $\omega(G)=\chi(G)$. A vertex $v\in V(G)$ is contained in a maximum clique of $G$ if it belongs to a clique of size $\omega(G)$.

**Vertex-maximum-clique criterion.** Any weakly perfect graph $G$ is a perfect graph if each vertex $v\in V(G)$ is in some maximum clique of $G$.

The claim proposes a sufficient condition for weak perfection to extend from the graph itself to every induced subgraph, which is the defining requirement for perfection. The supplied text gives no independent resolution or discussion of the claim; its status is therefore open.

337909.title: Refined Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture for Fourier–Jacobi periods
337909.literal_statement:
Let $F$ be a totally real number field, let $n'=n$ or $n'=n-1$, and let $\pi=\otimes'_v\pi_v$ and $\pi'=\otimes'_v\pi'_v$ be irreducible cuspidal automorphic representations with tempered $A$-parameters $\Psi$ and $\Psi'$, exactly one of which is genuine. Fix a sufficiently large finite set $S$ of bad places. **Refined Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture.** For every place $v$, the local Hom-space

$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Sp}_{n'}(F_v)}(\pi_v\otimes\pi'_v\otimes\overline{\omega_{\psi_{\xi,v}}},\mathbb{C})
$$

is nonzero if and only if the corresponding local period factor $\alpha_v$ is nonzero for suitable local vectors. Moreover, for factorizable vectors there is an explicit constant $\Delta^S$ such that

$$
|\mathcal{P}_{n,n',\psi_\xi}(\varphi,\varphi',\phi)|^2
=\frac{2\Delta^S}{|A_\Psi||A_{\Psi'}|}
\left.\frac{L^S(s,\pi\times\pi'\times\chi_\xi)}{L^S(s+1/2,\pi,\operatorname{Ad})L^S(s+1/2,\pi',\operatorname{Ad})}\right|_{s=1/2}
\prod_{v\in S}\alpha_v(\varphi_v,\varphi'_v,\phi_v).
$$

This refines the global Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture by predicting an exact factorization of the squared global period into an $L$-value, adjoint factors, and local periods. The source presents it as conjectural; the local integral's absolute convergence is known.

337930.title: Colored Erdős–Sós conjecture for trees with leaves of different colors
337930.literal_statement:
Let $T$ be a tree with $k$ edges. In its proper vertex $2$-coloring, assume that not all leaves have the same color. Let $\operatorname{ex}^c(n,T)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph for which every proper vertex coloring avoids a copy of $T$ whose leaves receive more than one color.

**Colored Erdős–Sós conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{ex}^c(n,T) \le \frac{(k-1)n}{2}.
$$

The conjecture is proposed as a strengthening of the Erdős–Sós conjecture for trees whose proper $2$-coloring has leaves of different colors. Its status is not specified in the supplied text.

337971.title: Univalence or typical reality of the multiplier function
337971.literal_statement:
Let $N$ and $T$ be positive integers, and let $\Phi(z)$ be the function constructed from the stabilization polynomials and the parameter $\gamma$.

**Univalence conjecture.** For any $N$ and $T$ there is a choice of $\gamma$ such that the function $\Phi(z)$ is univalent or typically real in $\mathbb D$. The largest value of $\gamma$ is a point of interest, since it produces the widest region for the multipliers.

If $\Phi$ is univalent or typically real, then its boundary image has only the two intersections with the real axis at $\Phi(1)=1$ and $\Phi(-1)$. This would yield estimates for the optimization problem and enlarge the region of multipliers for which the closed-loop system has a stable $T$-cycle. The source gives no resolution of the conjecture.

337987.literal_statement: Let $q$ be a power of $2$ and let $n=q^m+1$, with the quantities $\delta_2$ and $\delta_3$ defined as in the preceding cases for even $m$. **Second and third largest coset leader conjecture.** If $\delta_2$ and $\delta_3$ are given as above, then $\delta_2$ and $\delta_3$ are the second and third largest coset leaders, respectively. 337995.title: Subquadratic conjecture for odd cycles with an additional forbidden odd cycle
337995.literal_statement:
Let $k<l$ be positive integers, and let $ex(n,F,H)$ denote the maximum number of copies of $F$ in an $n$-vertex graph containing no copy of any graph in $H$.

**Subquadratic odd-cycle conjecture.** There exists an $\epsilon>0$ such that

$$
ex(n,C_{2k+1},{\mathscr C}_{2k}\cup\{C_{2l+1}\})=O(n^{2-\epsilon}).
$$

The source proves only a quadratic upper bound for this generalized Turán number and conjectures a power saving below $n^2$. The question concerns how strongly forbidding an additional odd cycle reduces the number of copies of an odd cycle.

338002.title: The affine DT4 vertex conjecture for solid partitions
338002.literal_statement:
Let $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3,\lambda_4$ be equivariant parameters subject to $\lambda_1+\lambda_2+\lambda_3+\lambda_4=0$. For every solid partition $\pi$, let $L_\pi(d_1,d_2,d_3,d_4)$ be the equivariant Euler-class contribution of the tautological bundle with weights $d_1,d_2,d_3,d_4$, and let $\mathsf{w}_\pi$ be the corresponding equivariant DT4 weight, defined up to sign. Let $M(q)$ denote the MacMahon function.

**The affine DT4 vertex conjecture.** There exists a way of choosing the signs of the weights $\mathsf{w}_\pi$ such that

$$
\sum_{\pi}L_\pi(d_1,d_2,d_3,d_4)\,\mathsf{w}_\pi q^{|\pi|}=M(-q)^{\frac{(d_1\lambda_1+d_2\lambda_2+d_3\lambda_3+d_4\lambda_4)(-\lambda_1\lambda_2\lambda_3-\lambda_1\lambda_2\lambda_4-\lambda_1\lambda_3\lambda_4-\lambda_2\lambda_3\lambda_4)}{\lambda_1\lambda_2\lambda_3\lambda_4}}.
$$

The identity is required to hold in $\frac{\mathbb{Q}(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3,\lambda_4)}{(\lambda_1+\lambda_2+\lambda_3+\lambda_4)}(d_1,d_2,d_3,d_4)[[q]]$, with the sum over all solid partitions. This is the local $\mathbb{C}^4$ vertex prediction underlying the toric DT4 correspondence; it is verified in the paper only to finite order in $q$.

338010.title: Triangle extremality conjecture for the graph \(\operatorname{BT}(3)\)
338010.literal_statement:
For $k\geq 2$, let $\widetilde{\operatorname{BT}}(k)$ be obtained from $T_2(2k)$ by deleting an edge and adjoining a new vertex to the two endpoints of that edge, and let

$$
\operatorname{BT}(k)=\widetilde{\operatorname{BT}}(k)\vee I_{k+1}.
$$

Let $f_3(\Delta,\omega)$ be the supremum of the triangle density $\rho_3$ among graphs with maximum degree at most $\Delta$ and clique number at most $\omega$. **Triangle extremality conjecture.** For $k=3$,

$$
f_3(2k+1,3)=\rho_3(\operatorname{BT}(k)).
$$

The preceding theorem proves that $\operatorname{BT}(k)$ beats the relevant Turán graph for $k=2,3$; the conjecture asserts its optimality in the case $k=3$, namely for parameters $(\Delta,\omega)=(7,3)$.

338016.title: The equal-slit-length conjecture for doubly-intruded hexagons
338016.literal_statement: Consider the scaling regime in which $x+y=y+t=z=N$, all fern lobe sizes are equal to $1$, both ferns have an even number of lobes, and their combined length is $m+n=M$. Let the regular hexagon have side length $M/2+N$, and suppose that, as the parameters tend to infinity, $M/(M/2+N)\to p$ with $0<p<2$, $x/(M/2+N)\to h$ with $0<h<1$, and $m/n\to r$. **Equal-slit-length conjecture.** For any given $0<p<2$ and any fixed $0<h<1$, the maximum occurs when $r_p=1$ $($i.e., when the slits have the same length$)$. This predicts that the number of lozenge tilings is maximized when the two intruding slits have equal lengths, although the problem remains open in the stated scaling regime.

338084.title: Eggleton–Erdős conjecture on subset sums of zero-sum free subsets
338084.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be an additive finite abelian group and let $S$ be a **zero-sum free subset** of $G$, meaning that no nonempty subsequence of $S$ has sum $0$. Write

$$
\Sigma(S)=\{\sigma(T)\mid T\text{ is a subsequence of }S\text{ with }1\leq |T|\leq |S|\}.
$$

**Eggleton–Erdős conjecture.** The set of subset sums satisfies

$$
|\Sigma(S)|\geq \left\lfloor\frac{1}{2}|S|^2\right\rfloor+1.
$$

Furthermore, this lower bound can be achieved by a zero-sum free subset $S$ of a cyclic group.

This conjecture concerns the minimum possible number of nonempty subset sums of a zero-sum free subset. The stated candidate is presented as a conjecture attributed to R. B. Eggleton and P. Erdős; its resolution is not established in the supplied text.

338146.title: Conjecture on the extremal degree power of broom-free graphs
338146.literal_statement:
Let $B_{\ell,s}$ be a broom graph, let $H(n,\ell)$ denote the graph used in the paper, and let $\operatorname{ex}_p(n,B_{\ell,s})$ be the maximum degree power among $B_{\ell,s}$-free graphs on $n$ vertices. **Broom degree-power conjecture.** For $p\ge 2$, $\ell\ge 6$, $s\ge 0$, and sufficiently large $n\ge n_0(\ell,s)$,

$$
\operatorname{ex}_p(n,B_{\ell,s})=e_p(H(n,\ell)).

338224.title: Minimum complexity conjecture for square-free ternary words
338224.literal_statement: Let ${\mathbf T}$ be the ternary Thue word, the fixed point of the morphism $0\mapsto012$, $1\mapsto02$, and $2\mapsto1$. 338227.title: Erdős–Kleitman minimum saturated-family conjecture
338227.literal_statement:
Let $s\geq 2$, let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ be **$s$-saturated** if it contains no $s$ pairwise disjoint sets and is maximal with respect to this property.

**Erdős–Kleitman's conjecture.** Every $s$-saturated family satisfies

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\geq (1-2^{-(s-1)})\cdot 2^n.
$$

The bound is attained by the family of all subsets of $[n]$ having nonempty intersection with $[s-1]$, so the conjecture asserts that this natural example is smallest. The claim concerns the minimum possible size of a maximal family avoiding $s$ pairwise disjoint sets.

338262.title: The minimum-weight dual-code characterization of the Desarguesian plane
338262.literal_statement:
Let $\pi$ be a projective plane of prime order $p$, and let $C_p^\perp(\pi)$ denote the dual of its $p$-ary code. For a codeword, its **Hamming weight** is the number of nonzero coordinates. **The minimum-weight dual-code conjecture.** The code $C_p^\perp(\pi)$ has at most

$$
p^2(p^3-1)\binom{p+1}{3}
$$

words of Hamming weight $3p-3$, and equality holds if and only if $\pi$ is isomorphic to $PG(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$. The claim is proposed as a coding-theoretic route toward the uniqueness conjecture for projective planes of prime order; no resolution is given in the supplied text.

338308.title: Three-subgraph regular-irregular decomposition conjecture
338308.literal_statement:
A subgraph is called **regular or locally irregular** according as it is regular or locally irregular. The regular-irregular number $\operatorname{reg\text{-}irr}(G)$ is the minimum number of subgraphs into which the edges of a graph $G$ can be decomposed, with every subgraph regular or locally irregular. **Three-subgraph regular-irregular conjecture.** Every graph can be decomposed into $3$ subgraphs, such that each subgraph is locally irregular or regular.

This conjecture weakens the conjecture that every non-exception graph has irregular chromatic index at most $3$ and strengthens the conjecture that every graph has regular-irregular chromatic index at most $2$. The supplied text does not report a resolution.

338311.title: The maximum-deviation limit conjecture for the Sine-beta counting process
338311.literal_statement:
Let $M_{\lambda,t}$ be the martingale process associated with the Sine$_\beta$ counting process, and let $M_{\lambda,\infty}$ denote its terminal value. For $x\geq 1$, consider the maximum over spectral parameters $0\leq \lambda\leq x$.

**Maximum-deviation limit conjecture.** There is a random variable $\xi$ such that

$$
\max_{0\leq \lambda\leq x}(M_{\lambda,\infty})-\frac{4}{\sqrt{\beta}}\left(\log x-\frac{3}{4}\log\log x\right) \xrightarrow[x\to\infty]{\mathrm{W}} \xi.
$$

This conjecture predicts a limiting distribution for the centered maximum deviation of the Sine$_\beta$ counting process. The supplied text motivates it through a Gaussian-process approximation and does not provide evidence of a resolution.

338329.title: Jablan–Radović conjecture on rational knots and OGC knots
338329.literal_statement:
A knot diagram is **straight** if, after labeling its $n$ crossings in traversal order, its knot word has the form

$$
(1,2,3,\ldots,n-1,n,\sigma(1),\sigma(2),\sigma(3),\ldots,\sigma(n-1),\sigma(n)),
$$

where $\sigma\in S_n$; a **straight number** $\mathtt{str}(K)$ is the minimum crossing number of a straight diagram of $K$. An OGC knot is a knot admitting a straight diagram, equivalently a diagram with a short OGC Gauss code. **Jablan–Radović conjecture.** Every rational knot is an OGC knot. The statement concerns whether the class of rational knots is contained in the class of knots admitting such straight diagrams; the source provides no resolution status.
338329.reason_and_next_lemma: Need actual source distinction between existence of straight diagrams and crossing-minimal OGC codes before treating rational-knot inclusion as new. No source-body review or proof claimed.

338405.title: Logarithmic bipartite induced subgraphs in triangle-free graphs
338405.literal_statement:
Let $d$ be a positive integer. A **triangle-free graph** is a graph containing no triangle, and a **bipartite induced subgraph** is an induced subgraph that is bipartite. **Triangle-free bipartite-subgraph conjecture.** There is a constant $C>0$ such that any triangle-free graph with minimum degree at least $d$ contains a bipartite induced subgraph of minimum degree at least

$$
C\log d.
$$

This is a quantitative variation of the clique-or-bipartite-induced-subgraph conjecture and would be sharp up to the choice of $C$ according to the source. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
338405.reason_and_next_lemma: Universal logarithmic bipartite induced minimum-degree bound; random cut gives bipartite subgraph, not induced bipartite subgraph. Missing independent-parts construction and degree retention.

338406.title: Girth-forces-dense-bipartite-induced-subgraph conjecture
338406.literal_statement: Let $d_0$ and $g_0$ be constants. A **bipartite induced subgraph** is an induced subgraph that is bipartite. **Girth-induced-subgraph conjecture.** There exist $d_0$ and $g_0$ such that any graph of girth at least $g_0$ with minimum degree at least $d_0$ contains a bipartite induced subgraph of minimum degree at least $3$. This is a high-girth specialization of the search for dense bipartite induced subgraphs in graphs of large minimum degree. The supplied text gives no resolution.
338406.reason_and_next_lemma: Existential d0,g0 constants cannot be refuted by a bounded small graph. Need unbounded-girth/high-degree obstruction family or full constructive theorem.

338407.title: Logarithmic separation choosability for bipartite graphs
338407.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite graph with maximum degree $\Delta$, and let $\operatorname{ch}_{\operatorname{sep}}(G)$ denote its separation choosability. **Alon–Krivelevich separation-choosability conjecture.** There is a constant $C>0$ such that

$$
\operatorname{ch}_{\operatorname{sep}}(G) \le C\log \Delta.
$$

This is the separation-choosability analogue of a conjecture of Alon and Krivelevich for ordinary choosability. The source explicitly states that both this conjecture and the original choosability conjecture remain open; if true, they would generalise the known upper bounds for complete regular bipartite graphs.
338407.reason_and_next_lemma: Maximum-degree1 log endpoint gives only routine domain correction, excluded. Intended asymptotic separation-choosability bound requires all separated list assignments; no full coloring mechanism.

338423.title: Strict monotone Hirsch conjecture for polytope orientations
338423.literal_statement: Let $P$ be a $d$-dimensional polytope with $n$ facets, and let ${\bf c}$ be a generic linear functional. Orient the graph of $P$ according to increasing values of ${\bf c}$, and denote this directed graph by $G(P,{\bf c})$. Its unique minimum and maximum vertices are called the source and sink, respectively. **Strict Monotone Hirsch Conjecture.** There is a directed path in $G(P,{\bf c})$ from the source of $P$ to the sink of $P$ of length at most $n-d$. The conjecture concerns a monotone analogue of the Hirsch bound and is presented as a stronger condition related to the face nonrevisiting question; the supplied text gives no resolution.
338423.reason_and_next_lemma: Corpus Santos snippet alone does not refute a source-to-sink directed path statement; ordinary Hirsch and strict monotone Hirsch are distinct. Primary counterexample body not read; no resolution claimed.

338430.title: Fici–Saarela minimum distinct abelian-square conjecture
338430.literal_statement:
For a binary linear word of length $n$, let $MDL(n)$ be the minimum number of distinct abelian squares it contains. **Fici–Saarela's conjecture.**

$$
MDL(n)=\lfloor n/4\rfloor,
$$

and the only words of length $4k+3$ containing exactly $k$ distinct abelian squares are $a^{2k+1}ba^{2k+1}$ and its complement. The conjecture gives both the sharp minimum and the stated equality cases for distinct abelian squares in binary words.

338430.reason_and_next_lemma: Actual Simpson Conj0.5 read, still conjectural in that body. Misattached1995 solved note concerns ordinary square avoidance. Circular successor does not solve linear bound. No new lower-bound proof.

338431.title: Minimum distinct abelian squares in circular binary words conjecture
338431.literal_statement:
For a circular binary word of length $n$, let $MDC(n)$ denote the minimum number of distinct abelian squares it contains. **The circular minimum conjecture.** The minimum number is

$$
\frac{n-1}{2}
$$

if $n$ is odd, and this bound is attained only by $a^n$, $a^{n-1}b$, and their complements and conjugates; if $n$ is even, the minimum is

$$
\frac{n-2}{2},
$$

and this bound is attained only by $a^kb^{n-k}$ and its complement and conjugates, where $k\in\{1,3,5,\dots,n-1\}$. The claim is presented as suggested by computer experiments, and the source gives no proof or resolution.

338434.title: Abelian Cayley graph bound implied by the Golomb–Welch conjecture
338434.literal_statement:
Let $AC(\Delta,k)$ be the largest order of an abelian Cayley graph of degree $\Delta$ and diameter $k$. For positive integers $d$ and $k$, the Lee-sphere cardinality is

$$
|S(d,k)|=\sum_{i=0}^{\min\{k,d\}}2^{i}\binom{k}{i}\binom{d}{i}.
$$

**Abelian Cayley graph bound.** For $k\ge2$ and $d\ge3$,

$$
AC(2d,k)<\sum_{i=0}^{\min\{k,d\}}2^{i}\binom{k}{i}\binom{d}{i}.
$$

This conjecture is presented as a consequence of the Golomb–Welch conjecture via the equivalence between linear perfect Lee codes and abelian Cayley graphs with degree $2d$, diameter $k$, and the corresponding number of vertices.
338434.reason_and_next_lemma: Full linear Golomb-Welch/abelian Cayley bound. Lee-ball cardinality alone is counting, not strict nonexistence. No group-ring contradiction for all d>=3,k>=2.

338441.title: Wilson's classification conjecture for nontrivially unstable circulants
338441.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a group and let $S$ be a nonempty inverse-closed subset of $G\setminus\{1\}$, where $1$ is the identity. The Cayley graph $\operatorname{Cay}(G,S)$ has vertex set $G$, with $x$ and $y$ adjacent exactly when $yx^{-1}\in S$. A circulant is a Cayley graph of a cyclic group; write it as $\operatorname{Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_n,S)$. Such a circulant is **nontrivially unstable** when it is unstable but does not fall under the trivial sources of instability described in the paper. Conditions (C.1)--(C.4) are the four conditions listed in the source: (C.1) $n$ is even and has an even divisor $a$ such that every even $s\in S$ also satisfies $s+a\in S$; (C.2) $n$ is divisible by $4$ and has an odd divisor $b$ such that every odd $s\in S$ also satisfies $s+2b\in S$; (C.3) $n$ is even and there is a subgroup $H\leq\mathbb{Z}_n$ for which $R:=\{j\bmod n\mid j\in S,\ j+H\not\subseteq S\}\neq\emptyset$, $D:=\gcd(R)>1$, and $j/D$ is odd for every $j\in R$; (C.4) $n$ is even and some integer $g$ coprime to $n$ satisfies $gs+n/2\in S$ for every $s\in S$. **Wilson's classification conjecture.** Every nontrivially unstable circulant $\operatorname{Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_n,S)$ satisfies at least one of (C.1)--(C.4). The conjecture proposes a classification of all nontrivially unstable circulants, but the paper notes that the proposed classification is false after correcting (C.2), and no conjectural classification is ultimately known.
338441.proof_body_review: Introduction conditions and corrected-condition example only; no full target proof review
338441.reason_and_next_lemma: Primary source explicitly refutes classification after replacing C2 by C2-prime. That does not itself refute original weaker C2 literal; keep logical distinction. Full original-conditions counterexample not supplied. No corrected-condition variant credit.

338464.title: The finite-variation stability conjecture
338464.literal_statement:
Consider a solution of the local length-minimization problem on a compact domain. Stability is tested using variational derivatives of the length functional.

**Finite-variation stability conjecture.** To determine whether the solution is stable over a compact domain, it suffices to examine derivatives of only finitely many orders.

The source gives an informal argument based on a bound on the domain diameter and remarks that analytic solvability of the induced partial differential equations may be needed. No rigorous resolution is supplied.
338464.reason_and_next_lemma: Informal stability claim lacks exact variation class, regularity, order bound and quantifiers. Smooth flat-function shortcut not justified for this length functional; no full-scope proof.
